column25: A new anti-data-center board voted Jan 2, 2024 to walk back the performance agreement signed weeks earlier. The dispute is pending in King George Circuit Court with trial rescheduled for September 2026, and a 7.5-hour June 2026 board meeting ended without a decision. column25: Tucson's council voted 7-0 on August 6, 2025 to rescind the planned annexation and development agreement, but the 290-acre site, county-owned land north of the Pima County Fairgrounds, was never inside the city, and the developer's June 2025 purchase agreement with Pima County predated the vote. Beale waived the annexation and city-water closing conditions, supervisors approved a revised deal 3-2 in December 2025, the sale closed December 24, 2025, and construction began April 24, 2026 under county-only approvals with state-permitted groundwater, reportedly scaled back and with Amazon stepping away as end user. The project never moved. The vote removed the city from the deal, along with its development agreement, reclaimed-water arrangement, and tax share. An opponents' lawsuit challenging the approval process was dismissed in April 2026.

column25: The 2M sq ft proposal for the closed Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill at 900 Conshohocken Road was withdrawn November 17, 2025 over a legal-standing defect (unfinalized agreement of sale), then resubmitted roughly six months later in spring 2026. Zoning hearing board proceedings were still underway and contentious as of a packed August 6, 2026 hearing, with the township council, county commissioners, and Governor Shapiro publicly opposed, and the developer has since filed a substantive validity challenge arguing the zoning ordinance fails to provide for data centers. No decision has been issued.

No relocation of the $19.2B Kingsboro project has been documented.

column25: Council denied Highlander SM One's ~200-acre rezoning 5-2 near 3 a.m. on February 18, 2026 after roughly nine hours of testimony, the site's second failed application since August 2025, then voted 4-3 on June 16, 2026 to remove data centers from every zoning district, making San Marcos the first Texas city with a citywide ban. The $1.5B figure is the project's reported potential valuation; no relocation has been documented, though a state senator has threatened a legal challenge to the ban itself.

column25: Commissioners approved the 829-acre, 900MW, $17B campus 3-2 on April 7, 2026, and nearly 20 residents sued in Coweta County Superior Court on May 5, 2026 to void the rezoning over procedural and wetlands-review claims. No court ruling had been reported as of early August 2026, and the county has separately kept a freeze on new data center applications.

column25: Commissioners approved the 1,848-acre Project Delta rezoning on January 12, 2026, then voided it in April 2026 after a March 12 SCSJ/SELC lawsuit exposed a defective hearing notice. The board rejected a recommended moratorium and re-opened a permitting path on July 13, 2026. The developer resubmitted the week of July 20, the planning board recommended denial of the new application on August 14, 2026, and the commissioners' public hearing is set for September 8, so nothing has been rebuilt or re-approved yet.
